nodes.name: Montane forest trees
nodes.desc: Podocarpus and other trees make up the montane forest on the volcano slopes, giving leaves, bark and fruit to monkeys, apes and elephants.

nodes.name: African alpine bamboo
nodes.desc: A bamboo belt grows on the volcano slopes at roughly 2,300 to 2,600 m. Gorillas move into it when fresh shoots appear.

nodes.name: Galium vines and forest herbs
nodes.desc: Galium vines are available all year in the high forest and are a staple food of mountain gorillas.

nodes.name: Savanna grasses
nodes.desc: Sacaton and other grasses cover the lava and Rutshuru plains and feed the large grazers of the lowland savanna.

nodes.name: Lake phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae in Lake Edward turn sunlight and dissolved nutrients into food for fish such as tilapia.

nodes.name: Mountain gorilla
nodes.desc: Eats mostly leaves, shoots and stems, with some bark and roots, and also giant senecio centres. The park protects about a third of the world population.

nodes.name: Mantled guereza
nodes.desc: A black-and-white leaf-eating monkey of the forest canopy. Chimpanzees and leopards prey on colobus monkeys.

nodes.name: Eastern chimpanzee
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats mainly fruit and leaves and also hunts monkeys such as colobus. Present in the park forests.

nodes.name: African bush elephant
nodes.desc: Grazes and browses on the savanna. Seeds from caper and wild cucurbit plants pass through its dung balls, spreading plants across the grassland.

nodes.name: Hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Rests in the lake and rivers by day and grazes on land at night. Its dung feeds tilapia, so falling hippo numbers hit the fishery.

nodes.name: African buffalo
nodes.desc: A big grass-eating herd animal of the central sector savanna, and a main prey of the lions there.

nodes.name: Uganda kob
nodes.desc: Thomas's kob is the abundant antelope of the Lake Edward plains. It grazes short grass and feeds lions, leopards and hyenas.

nodes.name: Nile tilapia
nodes.desc: The main fish of Lake Edward fishery. It eats algae and is fed by hippo dung; fish eagles and crocodiles eat it.

nodes.name: Spotted hyena
nodes.desc: A hunter and scavenger on the savanna, feeding on kills and on carcasses such as dead hippos.

nodes.name: African fish eagle
nodes.desc: A fish-eating raptor that perches along the lake shore and snatches tilapia from the surface.

nodes.name: Nile crocodile
nodes.desc: Lives along Lake Edward and the rivers. It eats fish, takes antelope at the water's edge and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Lion
nodes.desc: The park and Queen Elizabeth National Park in Uganda form one lion conservation unit. Lions need healthy kob and buffalo populations.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: A secretive forest and savanna hunter of monkeys, antelope and apes. Silverback gorillas defend their groups against it.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light on the open lake and the savanna drives the growth of algae and grass.

nodes.name: Rain and mist
nodes.desc: Frequent cloud and rain on the volcano slopes keep the montane forest, bamboo and vine zones growing.

nodes.name: Volcanic soils
nodes.desc: Eruptions of Nyiragongo and Nyamuragira spread ash and lava that weather into fertile soil for forest and grass.

nodes.name: Lake Edward and rivers
nodes.desc: The lake and the Rutshuru and other rivers hold the hippos, fish and crocodiles and feed the plankton.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects and microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the volcanic soil.
